text:
Alejandra: Hey team — OrchID is aiming to flip Dedicated capacity next Wednesday. Need final quota numbers and an autoscale plan. They expect a steady 800 qps peak with 20% burst allowance. :eyes:
Jeremy: Got it. Can you confirm 800 qps is per-region? Also do we have model fallback tiers configured?
Alejandra: Yes, US-west primary, EU fallback. Pricing tier is dedicated-tier-2. They asked for a plan that avoids hard 429s during load spikes.
Nisha: Ops note — current autoscale policy (scale_by_util) will add nodes at 70% GPU util. With their profile we might see 85% sustained without prefix cache. Recommend pre-warm + KV cache enabled.
Ben: I'll add a canary policy: start with two nodes, ramp to 6 over 15m, then vertical scale if average latency > 250ms for 1m. Also enable fallback to quantized variant model-q8 if latency crosses 400ms.
Alejandra: That sounds good. Tom (customer): Is the quantized model functionally identical? Any risk to result quality?
Tom: Quality loss is small on short prompts, we ran evals — avg rouge drop 0.6. Prefer to keep it as a safety net.
Jeremy: For load tests, propose this script (using k6):
```
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30m --rps 1200 script.js
```
and a burst phase:
```
k6 run --vus 400 --duration 5m --rps 2000 script-burst.js
```
Nisha: We'll deploy a traffic shadow to Dedicated for 48h before go-live. I'll also add Alerts: GPU_util > 85% for 2min, p95 latency > 500ms for 2min, 5xx > 1% for 5m.
Alejandra: Can we get a quick smoke test tomorrow 10:30 PT? Need SRE + CS + customer on the call.
Ben: I'm free. I'll push the canary config and post the rollout link.
Nisha: Same. I'll also enable KV cache with ttl=600s for the test.
Tom: Confirmed — we'll be on tomorrow. We'll run a small bespoke prompt set (50k requests) to validate model fidelity.
ops-bot: deploy-canary started by Ben at 1713506105 — canary id c-9832. Logs: https://internal.redwood/ci/c-9832
Alejandra: Thanks all. After smoke we'll capture feedback and finalize the renewal playbook with the customer. I'll add notes in the account health doc. :thumbsup:
